title: 4. Oracle SQL filtering, joins and keys
description: Oracle SQL joins and row filtering in the order shown in the Week 7 lecture.

items.question: Which ON condition does the slide use to match student alias se to sport alias sp?
items.explanation: The slide matches the sport number in the student table to the sport number in SPORT.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 9
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: How many rows are shown in the Week 7 INNER JOIN result?
items.explanation: The displayed inner join result contains eight rows. Students without a matching sport are not included.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 9
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: In the Week 7 student–sport example, what does LEFT JOIN with students on the left return?

options.text: All ten students, with NULL sport names for two
Eight assigned students plus three unused sports

items.explanation: The result retains all student rows, including the two whose sport name is missing.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 10
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: In the Week 7 example, students are on the left and sports are on the right. Which join keeps all sports but excludes students without a match?
items.explanation: SPORT is on the right. The right join keeps sports even when no student is enrolled.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 11
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: Which rows does a FULL OUTER JOIN preserve?

options.text: Matched rows and unmatched left rows only
Matched rows and unmatched right rows only
Matched rows and unmatched rows from both sides

items.explanation: A full outer join keeps matched rows and unmatched rows from both tables.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 7
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: What does SELECT * FROM products return in the slide example?
items.explanation: The slide uses SELECT * FROM products to retrieve all rows and all columns.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 14
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: Which filter selects products priced below 2.00, as in the lecture?
items.explanation: The slide uses WHERE price < 2.00 to select products priced below 2.00. The strict inequality excludes 2.00 itself.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 14
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: Which operator does the lecture use for a range filter that includes both endpoints?
items.explanation: BETWEEN expresses an inclusive range: values equal to the lower or upper limit are included.

references.label: Week 7 SQL, p. 20
references.file: reference/Oracle APEX/Week 7 - SQL Joins and Data Filtering 11Nov26.pdf

items.question: Which operator is used in the lecture’s string-pattern filter?
items.explanation: LIKE is used for string-pattern matching rather than exact equality or a numeric range.
